bullets.title: May NFP due: consensus ~85-90k, but sell-side models skew lower at 60-75k
bullets.body: Consensus for May nonfarm payrolls is ~85-90k with unemployment steady at 4.3% and AHE +0.3% MoM. JPMorgan and Goldman models are notably below at 75k and 60k respectively. Options market pricing ~1.0% SPX move on the print. 22V Research flags the regime shift: strong payrolls are now risk-OFF (inflation constraint), not risk-on — payrolls above 120k or AHE above 0.3% MoM would tighten financial conditions. Piper Sandler previews May CPI at 0.2% core (below 0.3% consensus), arguing tariff relief and airfare deflation keep inflation tame.

bullets.title: Global risk-off extends: Nasdaq futures -1.1%, Korea KOSPI -6%, semis leading lower
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures are down ~0.5-0.6% and Nasdaq futures down ~1.1% in pre-market Friday, extending Thursday's AVGO-driven selloff. Asia saw Korea KOSPI down 5.5-6% (sidecar circuit-breaker triggered), Taiwan TAIEX -2%, Nikkei -1.85%, and Europe Tech -1.8%. Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) declined ~3.4%. The backdrop includes USD/KRW hitting 17-year lows and Japan's 30-yr JGB yield above the comparable German bund.

bullets.title: AVGO's 'disappointing' AI guidance the proximate trigger; $285bn market cap rout
bullets.body: Broadcom's Q2 results showed AI segment revenue +143% YoY to $10.8bn and CEO guidance for Q3 AI chip revenue >$16bn (+200% YoY), yet markets sold the news as 'weaker than hoped.' The selloff cascaded to European semis (ASML -3%, SK Hynix -7%), and drove broad profit-taking after the MSCI World Semis index had surged ~50% in two months. JPM notes AVGO multi-GW customer commitments (Anthropic 1GW+, Meta 3GW, OpenAI) de-risk FY27/28, and Erste Group upgraded AVGO to Buy. Barclays flagged CTA and fast-money positioning may be losing steam.

bullets.title: NVIDIA HBM4 approved from all three memory suppliers; SoCAMM capacity cut due to pricing
bullets.body: NVIDIA completed HBM4 qualification from Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron for next-gen AI accelerators. Separately, NVIDIA reduced SoCAMM memory configuration on Vera Rubin NVL72 by ~50% (55TB to 28TB) due to elevated memory prices, though Meritz Securities notes total SoCAMM2 demand is increasing. Jensen Huang hinted at upcoming surprises during a Seoul visit where he met Hyundai, Samsung, and SK Group, and announced an R&D center in South Korea. He also called Marvell 'the next trillion-dollar company.'

bullets.title: DRAM prices surging; 2Q26 Server DRAM contracts +45-50% QoQ; NAND +20-30% in 3Q
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley memory update: 2Q26 server DRAM quotations increased 45-50% with Samsung potentially raising prices further in June. 3Q26 DRAM contracts expected +10-20% QoQ and NAND +20-30% QoQ as suppliers resist multi-year LTAs. BNP Paribas analyst now expects ASP peak mid-2026 (pulled forward from mid-2027), with QoQ declines starting early 2025. SK Hynix has no plans to add NAND capacity; only YMTC and Kioxia will expand. SK Hynix is also targeting doubling DRAM wafer capacity by 2030-2031 and its U.S. listing plan reportedly has 'tremendously positive' investor feedback.

bullets.title: BoJ rate hike June 16 increasingly priced in as Japan real wages beat for 4th straight month
bullets.body: Japan April cash earnings rose 3.5% YoY (vs. 3.1% consensus) and real wages +1.9% (vs. 1.7%), the fourth consecutive month of positive real income growth — the longest streak in five years. Markets now price a BoJ hike on June 16 with at least one more before year-end. USD/JPY held near 160 with Japan FM signaling readiness to intervene. The 30-year JGB yield is now above the equivalent German bund yield, and Japan's foreign reserves saw their largest monthly decline in May since 2000.

bullets.title: Fed neutral rate structurally higher; AI capex a key driver, threatening 2027 easing cycle
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises its neutral real policy rate estimate 50bp to 134bp over the past year, implying current Fed policy is neutral rather than restrictive. AI-related capex — driven by corporate investment cycles independent of the business cycle — is identified as the primary structural force pushing neutral rates higher. Higher neutral rates combined with firmer inflation are risks to the Fed normalization outlook for 2027.

bullets.title: Middle East/Iran war raises global CPI 1pp to 3.7%; Brent ~$100, but oil pulled back Thursday
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its 2026 global CPI forecast by 1 percentage point to 3.7%, with Brent crude expected around $100/bbl through year-end due to Strait of Hormuz disruption. However, Brent settled down 2.84% to $95/bbl Thursday as Iran-US ceasefire signals emerged, and Trump teased deal details including immediate Hormuz reopening. The Fed estimates a 33% oil shock now causes only 1.5% PCE impact (vs. 2.2% in the 1970s) as the US has become an oil exporter. ECB expected to hike twice in 2026 due to war-driven inflation.

bullets.title: S&P 500 near 10-week win streak; positioning stretched but CTA room to add on volatility decline
bullets.body: S&P 500 is on track for its longest weekly winning streak since 1985. S&P short interest is at a 10-year high. UBS notes leveraged NDX ETFs at ~70% of QQQ AUM create mechanical flow sensitivity. CTA exposures in ES1 and NQ1 are at 53rd and 58th percentile vs. 3-year average — room to buy if volatility drops. JPM's 4M Intraday Recovery Score has risen to 20%, needing 3 'good' days to turn bullish. Target Date Fund inflows hit +$18bn in the first 3 days of June vs. +$15bn in all of May.

bullets.title: AAPL WWDC June 8: Siri overhaul and Gemini integration framed as AI 'catch-up' not breakthrough
bullets.body: AAPL WWDC keynote is June 8 at 1pm ET. Citi and Jefferies both describe the event as an AI catch-up phase — major Siri overhaul using Google Gemini to close competitive gaps rather than a breakthrough. AAPL's 2.5B+ installed base and integrated ecosystem position it uniquely for edge AI monetization. AAPL's forward P/E is bumping against multi-year highs. Strong Mac Mini demand from agentic AI use cases (OpenClaw) signals early hardware traction, with potential monetization through software, developer tools, and AI-driven services.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO priced at $135/share; S&P declines fast-track inclusion, delaying ~$14B passive inflows
bullets.body: SpaceX IPO is fixed at $135/share (non-negotiable per banks), implying a ~$1.75T valuation, and could trade as early as June 12. S&P DJI concluded its megacap methodology review with no changes, meaning SpaceX will not be fast-tracked into the S&P 500 — delaying an estimated $14B in passive fund inflows by at least one year. Fidelity lowered the minimum investment to $2K from $500K, and SpaceX is offering up to 30% of the float to retail. FTSE Russell and Nasdaq indices have faster timelines. Tesla shareholders are reportedly getting a dedicated allocation.

bullets.title: Alphabet $84B equity raise is 'credit positive'; $4T AI IPO wave ahead includes Anthropic, OpenAI
bullets.body: Moody's called Alphabet's $84B equity raise credit positive. Roth and JPMorgan flag a forthcoming $4T AI IPO wave — SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI — that could enter the top 10 global tech valuations. Anthropic is calling for an industry-wide AI development pause (widely viewed as strategic). US officials have reportedly held talks about the government acquiring equity stakes in AI companies. The heavy equity supply pipeline is seen as a potential headwind for markets.

bullets.title: Korea: KOSPI -6%, 17-yr low for KRW; foreign equity outflows worst in history
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell 6% overnight (sidecar activated) and the Korean won hit a 17-year low vs. the dollar (~1,547 USD/KRW, approaching 2008 GFC highs). Foreigners have sold Korean stocks every single day since May 6 — the longest such streak on record — with domestic leveraged retail investors as the primary buyers. EM equity fund outflows accelerated to -$7.5B this week, led by Korea (-$7.5B) and India (-$4.1B).

bullets.title: TSMC extends order visibility to 2030; targets mid-30% revenue growth; CoWoS capacity raised to 180kwpm in '27
bullets.body: TSMC CEO C.C. Wei stated AI demand growth has surprised everyone including Jensen Huang, and that demand will take 'a very long time' to satisfy. TSMC now has visibility extending to 2030, an extraordinary horizon vs. the typical few-quarter window in an upcycle. Jefferies raises TSMC '27 CoWoS capacity to 180kwpm (from 170k), with supply-demand gap widening 15-20% in '27. TSMC targets mid-30% YoY revenue growth for the current year. High-NA EUV is in research/pilot phase, not yet mass production.

bullets.title: Strong payroll data is now a risk-OFF signal; inflation regime has replaced demand-weakness regime
bullets.body: 22V Research argues the market regime has decisively shifted: strong payrolls now signal risk-off because inflation (not demand) is the binding constraint. 10-year yields above 4.5% are headwinds for stocks and cyclicals. The 10-year term premium is well above post-GFC levels. JPM recommends reducing cyclical exposure after the May 15-29 rally (Airlines +19%, Retailers +10%), preferring a Tech/Cyclicals barbell hedged with VIX longs, NDX/RTY puts, and Energy commodity longs. FOMC cut probability is 3.6% at the June meeting.

bullets.title: AI boom at 'stage 6 of 10'; not 1999 — driven by capex and earnings, ends via excess investment
bullets.body: JPMorgan argues the current AI boom is mechanically at stage 6 of 10, fundamentally different from 1999 dot-com because it is driven by strong capex and earnings (not pure expectations). The boom will end via excess capital investment buildup, not demand collapse. AI equity gains are the primary current wealth effect driver (~0.3pp to consumption growth). Separately, Jefferies hosts Ed Zitron on June 30 to debate AI economics skepticism, and TSMC/Anthropic/OpenAI CEOs each acknowledge AI token costs are becoming a major enterprise pressure point.

bullets.title: Tech layoffs hit highest level since Aug 2024; 123K+ cuts YTD, up 65% vs 2025
bullets.body: US tech companies announced their highest monthly layoff total since August 2024, with YTD cuts exceeding 123,000 — up more than 65% versus the same period in 2025. 40% of recent layoffs are attributed to AI and automation. This includes Teradata freezing salary raises to fund AI investments and PENN Interactive laying off 75 workers with AI supporting flat-to-higher productivity. High-paying tech jobs are disproportionately affected.

bullets.title: Cloudflare: bot/AI traffic now 57.5% of HTML requests; agentic traffic surpassed human traffic
bullets.body: Cloudflare Radar data show bots and AI now account for 57.5% of all webpage requests on Cloudflare's network (handling ~20% of the internet). Agentic traffic has just surpassed human traffic, with the timeline compressing from 'end of 2027' to 'early 2027.' KeyBank models Cloudflare FY27 operating margin at 19.7% vs. consensus 16.6%, and notes Workers platform and security suite as AI winners. Cloudflare shares are up 34.6% YTD.

bullets.title: EU sovereignty requirements threaten US cloud/AI providers; US AI safety bill mandates audits
bullets.body: The EU is proposing cybersecurity revisions with sovereignty requirements that would limit non-EU cloud/AI provider access to critical infrastructure. Simultaneously, a bipartisan US draft bill would impose federal AI safety rules with mandatory risk disclosure and third-party audits. The US NSA is deploying Anthropic's Mythos AI for offensive cyber operations. Jane Street is building its own 100-200 MW data center.

bullets.title: JPM upgrades TSLA to Neutral; CRWD downgraded to Hold at Berenberg on valuation
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded Tesla to Neutral from Underweight. Berenberg downgraded CrowdStrike to Hold from Buy, citing valuation (PT raised to $720 from $525 with the stock at $719). BNP Paribas Exane downgraded Fiserv to Underperform with a $46 PT (18% downside from ~$55). Erste Group upgraded AVGO to Buy and TSLA to Hold; downgraded CBOE, CME, and WMT from Buy to Hold. Edgewater upgraded APP and Unity to Outperform.
